clue.text: Chubby person may have this clue to good health!

parts.note: the toast 'chin-chin' means good health, and it is one body-part word written twice over

explanation.surface: A cheery note that a plump person has a secret tip for staying well.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: write CHIN twice, giving CHIN-CHIN, a British drinking toast meaning 'good health!'. So the answer is a 'clue' to that toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold of fat beneath the jaw is a typical feature of a plump, heavy-set person.

clue.text: Anyhow I tend to follow an order, being this

definitions.text: Anyhow I tend to follow an order, being this

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the order, so they follow it

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: anyhow means in a random, careless way, so the letters of I tend are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who always obeys an order is, naturally, this way inclined.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: someone who follows an order.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tends to follow an order is dutiful and compliant, which is exactly the meaning.

clue.text: Save British Gas!

parts.note: Ar is the chemical symbol for argon, a gas

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to rescue British Gas, the UK energy company.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition meaning except, as in 'all bar one', it is a synonym of save.

clue.text: One presents medal on the radio

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is spoken, so the letters are said aloud

parts.note: the MC is the Military Cross, a British gallantry medal

explanation.surface: A broadcaster hands out a medal during a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the letters M C give the word for a master of ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies is the person who hosts and introduces a show, someone who presents.

clue.text: Part of phone Ned's lost in sou'wester?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go into the hat

parts.note: a sou'wester is a waterproof hat worn by sailors

indicators.note: lost means astray or confused, so the letters of Ned's are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man's mobile phone has gone missing inside his fishing hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges NEDS into NDSE, which goes 'in' HA-T. The question mark flags a sou'wester as just one example of a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The receiver held to ear and mouth is the component of a telephone you pick up.

clue.text: Resort a genuine winner at first for island

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters are rearranged
takes the opening letter of winner

explanation.surface: A holiday resort proves a real success, a true winner for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' is read as re-sort: shuffle A GENUINE with W, the first letter of 'winner'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the large Pacific landmass north of Australia, split between Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.

clue.text: Slough is in Berks, he declared

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone states that the town of Slough is in Berkshire, the English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the town (it is in Berkshire, a county west of London) but it is a verb meaning cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: To slough skin is to cast it off, as a snake does; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Drove one crazy, being sloppy

parts.note: drove someone mad is sent someone mad
I is the Roman numeral for one
mental is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone drove a companion mad by being careless and untidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy can mean mawkish or gushing, overly soft and emotional in feeling.

clue.text: Funny you feel no love for good-looker

indicators.note: funny means odd or strange, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no love means the letter for love is dropped

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: An odd confession: you feel no affection for an attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O ('no love') from YOU FEEL and 'Funny' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal term for an attractive person, someone well worth looking at.

clue.text: Hall perhaps is able to provide container

parts.note: Jerry Hall is a well-known American model, an example of someone named Hall
can means is able

explanation.surface: Perhaps a hall is capable of supplying a storage container.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-sided metal can for fuel or water, a kind of container.

clue.text: Stray bird seen around noon

indicators.note: the bird is placed around the letter for noon

parts.note: a wader is a long-legged wading bird such as a heron

explanation.surface: A lost bird was spotted at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to roam or drift away from a path, a synonym verb.

clue.text: Responsible and trustworthy? That's not on

indicators.note: says the word for on is to be absent from the longer word

parts.note: reliable means trustworthy
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A question whether being responsible and trustworthy is fair, answered with a disapproving 'that's not on'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not on' tells you to remove RE ('on', as in 're: your letter') from RELIABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally answerable or accountable for something, as in liable for damages.

clue.text: What those casting Dr Strangelove did for retailers?

definitions.text: What those casting Dr Strangelove did
definitions.meaning: the casting team hired Peter Sellers, the actor who played the title role
shop owners selling volumes of print

explanation.surface: A puzzle over what the film's casting team did for shopkeepers.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Sellers starred in Dr Strangelove, so its casting team had to engage him; the answer split as two words describes that.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops selling printed volumes are retail traders in a particular kind of goods.

clue.text: Bad team squeezes 1-0 with United

indicators.note: the team grips the other letters inside it

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club
the figures read as the letters I and O
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A weak team scrapes a narrow 1-0 win over United.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; '1-0' is read as I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: False or counterfeit, not genuine; bad in the sense of fake.

clue.text: Among pub cricket eleven's openers, struggle for lack of fitness

indicators.note: the word for struggle goes among the other letters

parts.note: an inn is a pub
to compete is to struggle against rivals

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A pub cricket team's opening batsmen struggle because they are out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: COMPETE goes 'Among' INN plus C and E (the 'openers' of cricket and eleven's).
explanation.definitionFit: Being unfit for a task means lacking ability or skill, the sense of fitness here.

clue.text: Game pies are cooked with chestnut stuffing

indicators.note: the letters for chestnut are stuffed inside the others
cooked means doctored or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ch is the racing abbreviation for chestnut, a horse colour

explanation.surface: Game pies are prepared with a chestnut stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like meat for the pies but is the definition: a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a board game, the American version of the Indian pastime pachisi.

clue.text: Flirt wants something to eat right away

indicators.note: the letter for right is taken away

parts.note: a croquette is a fried roll of food coated in breadcrumbs

explanation.surface: A flirt is hungry and wants a snack at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'immediately' but here takes R out of CROQUETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who flirts playfully, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Peanuts for one to carry in prepared portions

indicators.note: the word for carry goes in the rearranged letters
prepared means made ready, so the letters of portions are reworked

parts.note: to cart is to carry

explanation.surface: Peanuts are handed out for someone to carry, in prepared portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peanuts' looks like snacks but is the Charles Schulz comic featuring Charlie Brown and Snoopy.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts is an example of a comic told in a sequence of panels in a newspaper.

clue.text: Make solemn affirmation for trial

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Someone takes a solemn oath at a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense, to declare or assert solemnly, as in protesting one's innocence.

clue.text: Look round entertaining bachelor's summerhouse

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the other letters hold the bachelor's letter

parts.note: to gaze is to look
O is round in shape
B is the abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: Look around a summerhouse where a bachelor is entertaining guests.
explanation.definitionFit: An open garden pavilion with a view, a kind of summerhouse.

clue.text: Dance with lout without a fuss

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter a is dropped

parts.note: a yahoo is a boorish lout

explanation.surface: Someone attends a dance with a lout and there is no fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy commotion and hype, an informal synonym for fuss.

clue.text: Material prowess has importance ultimately for adult

indicators.note: the last letter of importance stands in for the letter for adult

parts.note: valour is bravery, prowess in battle
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: takes the final letter of importance

explanation.surface: A statement that bravery has material importance in the end for a grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: E (importance 'ultimately') goes in 'for' A (adult) in VALOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A plush fabric with a soft pile, a kind of cloth or material.

clue.text: Drip's taken up with a treacherous sort

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an IV is an intravenous drip
per means a, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: A drip, a feeble person, has got involved with a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drip' suggests a feeble person but is a medical IV, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous snake, and figuratively a spiteful or treacherous person.

clue.text: Withdraw and give up again?

parts.note: re- as a prefix means again
to cede is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: Someone retreats and surrenders once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To move back or pull away, as a tide does; a synonym of withdraw.

clue.text: Hasten, being late, and change in gym

parts.note: ex means former, late, as in an ex-wife

indicators.note: the word for change goes in the gym letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, gym at school
to edit is to change

explanation.surface: Hurry up, you are late, and get changed in the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed something up or make it happen sooner; a verb synonym for hasten.

clue.text: Cook keeps close to au pair

indicators.note: the word for cook holds that letter inside

parts.note: to do or cook food is to prepare it

indicators.note: close means the end, so the close of au is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cook stays near to the au pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'au pair' looks like one phrase, but 'au' supplies U and 'pair' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people working together, a twosome or pair.

clue.text: Excellent jam is sent back

indicators.note: sent back means returned the way it came, so the word for jam is read backwards

parts.note: to be in a spot is to be in a jam, a difficult situation

explanation.surface: An excellent jam is returned to the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal adjective meaning the best, as in 'that film is the best'.

clue.text: Meddler put in ground rule about pole dancing

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and rearrange

explanation.surface: A busybody is buried after a rule on pole dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder who interferes in the affairs of others, a meddling outsider.
